title: Primitive facets and interior lattice witnesses for a sharp saturated cone
statement:
Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated additive commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], sharp in the sense that $0$ is its only invertible element. Put $G=P^{m gp}$, $V=G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, and let $\sigma$ be the rational cone generated by $P$. Use the notions of facet and primitive normal in [def-trf-complete-toric-model]. Then $G$ is free abelian of finite rank and embeds in $V$, $\sigma$ is pointed and spans $V$, and $P=\sigma\cap G$. The facets form a finite set $\mathcal F$. Each $F\in\mathcal F$ has a unique surjective homomorphism $
u_F:G	o\mathbf Z$ nonnegative on $P$ whose rational extension has zero locus $F$ in $\sigma$. Moreover,
$$\sigma=\{v\in V:
u_F(v)\ge0	ext{ for every }F\in\mathcal F\}.$$
For each $F$ there exists $f_F\in P\cap F$ with $
u_H(f_F)>0$ for every $H
e F$. If $G=0$ then $P=\{0\}$, $V=\sigma=0$ and $\mathcal F=\varnothing$. If $\dim V>0$, there are nonzero rational forms $h_i$ indexed by a nonempty finite set $I$, and finitely many $a_j\in P$ generating $\sigma$, such that the inequalities $h_i\ge0$ give an irredundant description of $\sigma$, $x_0=\sum_j a_j$ satisfies $h_i(x_0)>0$ for every $i$, and $i\mapsto\sigma\cap\ker h_i$ is a bijection onto $\mathcal F$. For each $i$ there is $x_i\in\sigma\cap\ker h_i$ with $h_j(x_i)>0$ for $j
e i$ and $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}(\sigma\cap\ker h_i)=\ker h_i$. Each $
u_F$ is a positive rational multiple of its corresponding $h_i$, and the witnesses $f_F$ may be obtained as positive integral multiples of these $x_i$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-sharp-cone-lattice-intersection] to the given sharp finitely generated integral saturated monoid $P$. It gives the finite free lattice $G\subset V$, pointedness and spanning of $\sigma$, and $P=\sigma\cap G$. Choose finite monoid generators $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in P$; they generate the same rational cone by expanding each element of $P$. If $G=0$, injectivity gives $P=\{0\}$ and $V=\sigma=0$. No nonzero rational linear form exists on $V=0$, so the facet definition in [def-trf-complete-toric-model] gives no facets; all remaining assertions are vacuous or the equality $0=0$. Henceforth put $d=\dim V>0$.

proof.text: The finite free lattice makes $V$ finite-dimensional. Apply [lem-trf-rational-cone-dual-finite] to the finite list $a_j$ in $V$ to obtain finitely many rational linear forms whose simultaneous nonnegative locus is $\sigma$. Remove zero forms, which impose no condition, and then remove a redundant inequality whenever deleting it leaves that locus unchanged. The number of remaining inequalities strictly decreases, so this terminates with a finite irredundant family $(h_i)_{i\in I}$ of nonzero forms defining $\sigma$.

source.place: Agent-written expansion of the retained facet-valuation argument, old steps 1--5 in coord/reports/Q138/lem-trf-complete-toric-facet-valuations.md. Expose VI 1.6, printed p. 70, supplies the model context only, not this cone theorem.

proof.text: Every $h_i$ is nonnegative on $\sigma$, in particular on each $a_j$. Set $x_0=\sum_j a_j$. If $h_i(x_0)=0$, every nonnegative summand $h_i(a_j)$ is zero, so $h_i$ vanishes on $\sigma$ and its span $V$, contradicting $h_i\ne0$. Thus every $h_i(x_0)>0$. Also $I\ne\varnothing$: otherwise $\sigma=V$, whence pointedness gives $V=\sigma\cap(-\sigma)=\{0\}$, contradicting $d>0$.

proof.text: Fix $i\in I$. Irredundancy gives $y_i\in V$ with $h_j(y_i)\ge0$ for $j\ne i$ and $h_i(y_i)<0$; otherwise deleting $i$ would preserve the locus. Put $A=h_i(x_0)>0$, $B=h_i(y_i)<0$, $\alpha=-B/(A-B)\in(0,1)$ and $x_i=\alpha x_0+(1-\alpha)y_i$. Direct evaluation gives $h_i(x_i)=0$ and $h_j(x_i)>0$ for $j\ne i$, since the coefficient of $x_0$ is positive. Thus $x_i\in F_i:=\sigma\cap\ker h_i$. All these vectors and coefficients are rational.

proof.text: Conversely let $F=\sigma\cap\ker h$ be any facet as in [def-trf-complete-toric-model], with $h\ne0$ nonnegative on $\sigma$. Put $J=\{j:h(a_j)=0\}$. In a nonnegative expression $z=\sum_j q_j a_j\in F$, the equality $0=h(z)=\sum_j q_jh(a_j)$ forces $q_j=0$ whenever $h(a_j)>0$. Consequently $F$ is exactly the rational cone generated by the $a_j$ with $j\in J$. Put $a=\sum_{j\in J}a_j\in F$, allowing the empty sum.

proof.text: Some $h_i(a)$ must vanish. Indeed suppose all are positive. Since $h\ne0$, choose $v\in V$ with $h(v)=-1$, by rescaling a vector where $h$ is nonzero. Let $\epsilon$ be the minimum of $\{1\}\cup\{h_i(a)/(2|h_i(v)|):h_i(v)\ne0\}$. All entries are positive rational numbers. Then $h_i(a+\epsilon v)>0$ for all $i$, so $a+\epsilon v\in\sigma$, but $h(a+\epsilon v)=-\epsilon<0$. This contradicts nonnegativity of $h$ on $\sigma$.

proof.text: Choose $i$ with $h_i(a)=0$. The summands $h_i(a_j)$ for $j\in J$ are nonnegative, so each is zero. Step 6 gives $F\subseteq\ker h_i$. Since $F$ spans a $(d-1)$-dimensional space by the facet definition and both $\ker h$ and $\ker h_i$ are hyperplanes, $\operatorname{span}F=\ker h=\ker h_i$. Therefore $F=\sigma\cap\ker h=F_i$. Together with Step 5 this proves that $i\mapsto F_i$ is a bijection onto the facets, and hence that $\mathcal F$ is finite.

source.place: Agent-written expansion of the retained facet-valuation argument, old steps 1--5 in coord/reports/Q138/lem-trf-complete-toric-facet-valuations.md. Expose VI 1.6, printed p. 70, supplies the model context only, not this cone theorem.

proof.text: For each $i$, choose a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis $e_k$ of $G$ from Step 1 and a positive integer $N$ clearing the denominators of the finitely many $h_i(e_k)$. The nonzero homomorphism $\phi(g)=Nh_i(g)$ has integer values. Its image subgroup $S\subseteq\mathbf Z$ contains a positive integer; let $b$ be the least positive one. For $s\in S$, integer division writes $s=qb+r$, $0\le r<b$; then $r=s-qb\in S$, so minimality forces $r=0$. Hence $S=b\mathbf Z$. Define $\nu_{F_i}(g)=\phi(g)/b$. This is integral and surjective, extends to $(N/b)h_i$ on $V$, is nonnegative on $P$, and has zero locus $F_i$ in $\sigma$. Positive rescaling preserves every inequality, so the $\nu_{F_i}\ge0$ cut out $\sigma$.

proof.text:
Let $\mu:G	o\mathbf Z$ be another surjective nonnegative normal of $F_i$, and let $ ar\mu$ be its rational extension. Since $\operatorname{span}F_i=\ker h_i$, its nonzero extension has $\ker ar\mu=\ker h_i=\ker
u_{F_i}$. Choose $g_0\in G$ with $
u_{F_i}(g_0)=1$. For $v\in V$, $v-
u_{F_i}(v)g_0$ lies in that kernel, so $ ar\mu(v)=c
u_{F_i}(v)$, where $c=\mu(g_0)\in\mathbf Z$. At $x_0$ the first form is nonnegative and the second strictly positive; nonzeroness forces $c>0$. Surjectivity of $\mu$ now gives $c\mathbf Z=\mathbf Z$, hence $c=1$ and $\mu=
u_{F_i}$.

proof.text: Write each $x_i$ in the rational coordinates of the finite lattice basis from Step 9, and multiply by a positive common denominator $M_i$ to obtain $f_{F_i}=M_i x_i\in G$. It remains in $\sigma$, so $P=\sigma\cap G$ from [lem-trf-sharp-cone-lattice-intersection] gives $f_{F_i}\in P\cap F_i$. For $j\ne i$, $\nu_{F_j}(f_{F_i})=(N_j/b_j)M_i h_j(x_i)>0$. Thus these are precisely the required lattice witnesses and are positive integral multiples of the stated $x_i$. In dimension one the unique facet is $\{0\}$ and the construction permits $x_i=f_{F_i}=0$, since there are no other facets on which positivity is required.

b) ∧ (∀ g : Lattice P, (1 : ℚ) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] g ∈ cone P ↔ ∃ p : P, latticePoint p = g) ∧ Set.Finite {F : Set (RationalSpace P) | IsFacet P F} ∧ (∃ (ν : Facet P → Lattice P →+ ℤ) (h : Facet P → RationalSpace P →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ), (∀ F : Facet P, IsPrimitiveNormal F (ν F) ∧ (∀ μ : Lattice P →+ ℤ, IsPrimitiveNormal F μ → μ = ν F) ∧ IsRationalExtension (ν F) (h F) ∧ F.val = {v | v ∈ cone P ∧ h F v = 0}) ∧ (cone P : Set (RationalSpace P)) = {v | ∀ F : Facet P, 0 ≤ h F v} ∧ (∀ F : Facet P, ∃ f : P, rationalPoint f ∈ F.val ∧ ∀ H : Facet P, H ≠ F → 0 < ν H (latticePoint f)) ∧ ((∀ g : Lattice P, g = 0) → (∀ p : P, p = 0) ∧ (∀ v : RationalSpace P, v = 0) ∧ (cone P : Set (RationalSpace P)) = ({0} : Set (RationalSpace P)) ∧ IsEmpty (Facet P)) ∧ ((∃ v : RationalSpace P, v ≠ 0) → ∃ (s m : ℕ) (I : Fin s → RationalSpace P →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ) (a : Fin m → P) (x₀ : RationalSpace P) (e : Fin s ≃ Facet P) (x : Fin s → RationalSpace P), 0 < s ∧ (∀ i : Fin s, I i ≠ 0) ∧ (cone P : Set (RationalSpace P)) = {v | ∀ i : Fin s, 0 ≤ I i v} ∧ (∀ i : Fin s, ∃ v : RationalSpace P, (∀ j : Fin s, j ≠ i → 0 ≤ I j v) ∧ I i v < 0) ∧ (cone P : Set (RationalSpace P)) = ConvexCone.hull ℚ (Set.range (fun j : Fin m ↦ rationalPoint (a j))) ∧ x₀ = ∑ j : Fin m, rationalPoint (a j) ∧ (∀ i : Fin s, 0 < I i x₀) ∧ (∀ i : Fin s, (e i).val = {v | v ∈ cone P ∧ I i v = 0}) ∧ (∀ i : Fin s, x i ∈ cone P ∧ I i (x i) = 0 ∧ (∀ j : Fin s, j ≠ i → 0 < I j (x i)) ∧ Submodule.span ℚ ((e i).val) = LinearMap.ker (I i)) ∧ (∀ i : Fin s, ∃ c : ℚ, 0 < c ∧ h (e i) = c • I i) ∧ (∀ i : Fin s, ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : P), 0 < n ∧ rationalPoint f ∈ (e i).val ∧ (∀ H : Facet P, H ≠ e i → 0 < ν H (latticePoint f)) ∧ rationalPoint f = n • x i)))
